A display device may include a display panel, a power delivery network, an image controller, and a power delivery network (PDN) controller.

The display panel may include a plurality of sub-panels. Each of the sub-panels may receive one or more voltages delivered from the power delivery network. The delivery of the voltages to the respective sub-panels may be performed according to a control signal. In this manner, power supplied to different regions of the display panel can be controlled based on operating conditions of the display device.

The power delivery network may generate state information associated with the delivery of power to the display panel. The state information may include information indicating a current state, load condition, voltage delivery condition, or other operating status of the power delivery network. The generated state information may be used to determine the control signal that controls voltage delivery to the plurality of sub-panels.

The image controller may store frame image data corresponding to one or more image frames to be displayed on the display panel. The image controller may determine a number of frames to be integrated based on a window size. Using the determined number of frames, the image controller may generate integrated image data by integrating frame image data over the corresponding window. The integrated image data may represent image characteristics accumulated or combined across multiple frames.

The PDN controller may receive the state information from the power delivery network and the integrated image data from the image controller. Based on the state information and the integrated image data, the PDN controller may generate the control signal for controlling voltage delivery by the power delivery network. The PDN controller may also generate a size adjusting signal. The size adjusting signal may be provided to the image controller to adjust the window size used to determine how many frames are integrated. Accordingly, the display device can adaptively control both the voltage delivery operation of the power delivery network and the integration window used for image data processing.
outputs.L4:
A display device is provided that includes a display panel divided into a plurality of display sub-panels, a power delivery network configured to supply operating voltages to the respective sub-panels, an image controller configured to process image data for display, and a power delivery network controller configured to control voltage delivery based on display and power conditions. The display device may manage the voltages supplied to the different sub-panels by analyzing frame image data and power delivery network state information, thereby allowing voltage control to be adapted according to the image content being displayed and the electrical condition of the power delivery network.

In operation, the image controller receives frame image data corresponding to an image frame to be displayed on the display panel. The image controller integrates, accumulates, or otherwise processes the frame image data according to a window having an adjustable window size. The window may correspond to a region of the display panel, a group of pixels, or one or more display sub-panels. By changing the size of the window, the system can vary the granularity at which image data is analyzed. For example, a smaller window may provide more localized information regarding image brightness or load demand, while a larger window may reduce processing complexity and provide broader regional power information.

The power delivery network controller receives power delivery network state information, such as voltage levels, current levels, load conditions, voltage droop, resistance-related losses, temperature information, or other operating parameters associated with the power delivery network. The controller also receives integrated image data generated by the image controller. Based on the power delivery network state information and the integrated image data, the power delivery network controller generates one or more control signals for controlling voltage delivery to the display sub-panels. These control signals may adjust voltage levels, regulate power converters, compensate for voltage drops, or otherwise modify the manner in which power is supplied to different regions of the display panel.

The power delivery network controller may also generate a size-adjustment signal for adjusting the window size used by the image controller. The size-adjustment signal may be determined according to current display conditions, image content, power delivery limitations, or detected changes in the power delivery network state. For example, when the power delivery network indicates a localized voltage drop or increased load in a particular region, the controller may reduce the window size to obtain more detailed image information for that region. Conversely, when the display load is relatively uniform or stable, the controller may increase the window size to reduce computational overhead.

By coordinating image-data integration with real-time power delivery network monitoring, the display device can adaptively control the voltages supplied to multiple display sub-panels. This approach enables improved power management, more efficient voltage regulation, reduced unnecessary power consumption, and enhanced display performance. In particular, the system may help maintain stable luminance, reduce display artifacts caused by voltage variation, and support more reliable operation of high-resolution or large-area display panels in which power distribution conditions can vary across different regions of the panel.

A well-designed PDN, or Power Delivery Network, helps deliver clean and reliable power to every component that needs it. The quality of the PDN can directly affect signal integrity, reduce noise, and improve the overall reliability of the device.

When the provided PDN is carefully planned, engineers can minimize voltage drops, manage current flow, and prevent unwanted interference. counterfactuals.prompt: Create an invention disclosure summary for a display device in which a PDN controller receives state information from a power delivery network and integrated image data from an image controller to control voltages delivered to multiple display sub-panels.
counterfactuals.output:
## Invention Disclosure Summary

### Title  
**Display Device with Power Delivery Network Controller for Sub-Panel Voltage Control Based on Power State and Image Data**

### Technical Field  
This disclosure relates to electronic display devices and, more particularly, to power management for displays having multiple display sub-panels. The invention concerns coordinated control of voltages supplied to display sub-panels using power delivery network state information and image data.

### Background  
Modern display devices, including large-format displays, foldable displays, tiled displays, and high-resolution OLED, microLED, miniLED, LCD, or other emissive or transmissive displays, may be divided into multiple display sub-panels or regions. Each sub-panel may have different power requirements depending on displayed content, brightness, refresh rate, local dimming operation, thermal conditions, and electrical loading.

Conventional display power delivery systems often provide fixed or globally regulated supply voltages to the display panel or adjust power rails based only on limited load feedback. Such approaches may result in excess power consumption, voltage droop, localized thermal stress, reduced brightness uniformity, or inefficient headroom in voltage regulators. Additionally, image-based power variation across different display regions may not be sufficiently coordinated with real-time power delivery network conditions.

### Summary of the Invention  
The disclosed invention provides a display device including a power delivery network, an image controller, and a power delivery network controller. The display includes multiple display sub-panels, each configured to receive one or more controlled supply voltages. The image controller processes image data and provides integrated image data, such as luminance information, brightness maps, gray-level statistics, local dimming data, expected current consumption, refresh data, or other content-derived power demand indicators.

The power delivery network controller receives:  

1. **State information from the power delivery network**, such as voltage levels, current levels, regulator status, temperature, impedance, droop conditions, load transients, available power budget, or fault information; and  
2. **Integrated image data from the image controller**, representing content-dependent power requirements for one or more display sub-panels.

Based on both inputs, the power delivery network controller determines and controls voltages delivered to the multiple display sub-panels. The controller may independently adjust voltages for different sub-panels, coordinate voltage transitions, compensate for predicted loading, reduce unnecessary voltage headroom, and maintain brightness or image quality while improving power efficiency and reliability.

### Example System Architecture  
The display device may include:

- A display panel divided into a plurality of display sub-panels;
- A power delivery network configured to provide one or more supply voltages to the sub-panels;
- Voltage regulators, converters, switches, or power management circuits associated with respective sub-panels or groups of sub-panels;
- An image controller configured to receive image data and generate integrated image data associated with expected display operation;
- Sensors or monitoring circuits configured to generate power delivery network state information; and
- A power delivery network controller configured to generate voltage control signals for the power delivery network.

The integrated image data may be generated per frame, per sub-frame, per region, per sub-panel, or over a prediction window. The power delivery network controller may use the integrated image data to predict future sub-panel power demand and may use the power delivery network state information to correct, limit, or optimize voltage delivery in real time.

### Operation  
In one embodiment, the image controller analyzes incoming image frames and determines a brightness or load profile for each sub-panel. The image controller sends integrated image data to the power delivery network controller. The power delivery network simultaneously reports state information, including actual output voltage, load current, thermal conditions, and regulator capability.

The power delivery network controller then determines a target voltage for each sub-panel. For example, a sub-panel displaying a bright region may receive a higher supply voltage or increased regulator headroom, while a sub-panel displaying a dark or low-load region may receive a reduced voltage. If the power delivery network reports voltage droop or thermal stress, the controller may adjust one or more sub-panel voltages, stagger voltage transitions, limit brightness, or prioritize certain display regions.

### Potential Embodiments  
The invention may be implemented in various forms, including:

1. **Per-Sub-Panel Voltage Scaling**  
   Each display sub-panel receives an independently controlled voltage based on local image content and measured power delivery conditions.

2. **Predictive Voltage Control**  
   The controller uses integrated image data from upcoming frames to pre-adjust sub-panel voltages before high-brightness or high-current content is displayed.

3. **Closed-Loop Power Compensation**  
   The controller combines predicted image-based loading with measured PDN feedback to correct voltage droop, compensate for supply impedance, and improve luminance uniformity.

4. **Thermal-Aware Voltage Management**  
   The controller reduces or redistributes voltage delivery when state information indicates elevated temperatures in a regulator, conductor, connector, or sub-panel region.

5. **Power Budget Enforcement**  
   The controller allocates available power among sub-panels based on image importance, brightness requirements, user settings, or operating mode.

6. **Transition Coordination**  
   The controller staggers or shapes voltage changes among sub-panels to reduce inrush current, electromagnetic interference, visible artifacts, or power rail instability.

7. **Fault or Degradation Response**  
   If the PDN state information indicates a fault, undervoltage, overcurrent, or regulator limitation, the controller modifies voltages and may instruct the image controller to alter displayed content or brightness.

### Advantages  
The disclosed display device may provide one or more of the following advantages:

- Reduced power consumption by lowering unnecessary voltage headroom;
- Improved voltage regulation for high-dynamic-range or high-brightness content;
- Better luminance uniformity across display sub-panels;
- Reduced voltage droop and transient artifacts;
- Improved thermal management and component reliability;
- More efficient use of available power budget;
- Faster response to changing image content;
- Coordinated control between image processing and power delivery;
- Scalability for large, tiled, foldable, or segmented displays.

### Novel Aspects  
A key inventive aspect is the combined use of power delivery network state information and integrated image data to control voltages supplied to multiple display sub-panels. Rather than controlling display power solely from electrical feedback or solely from image content, the power delivery network controller integrates both real-time PDN conditions and content-derived demand information to determine sub-panel-specific voltage delivery.

### Example Claim Concepts  
1. A display device comprising multiple display sub-panels, a power delivery network, an image controller configured to generate integrated image data, and a power delivery network controller configured to receive state information from the power delivery network and the integrated image data and control voltages delivered to the display sub-panels.

2. The display device of claim 1, wherein the voltages are independently controlled for respective display sub-panels based on predicted current demand derived from the integrated image data.

3. The display device of claim 1, wherein the state information includes at least one of voltage, current, temperature, regulator status, power budget, or fault condition information.

4. The display device of claim 1, wherein the power delivery network controller adjusts voltages prior to display of an image frame based on integrated image data for the image frame.

5. The display device of claim 1, wherein the power delivery network controller coordinates voltage transitions among the multiple display sub-panels to reduce transient loading or display artifacts.
